Local Autonomy Index (1990–2020) and Regional Authority Index (1950–2018), scaled 0–1

The Local Autonomy Index project calculates an indicator of the political, policy and fiscal autonomy of local government in a range of Global North countries. The composite indicator is shown for 1990–2020.

The fiscal dimension of the LAI combines four sub-indicators: fiscal autonomy (independent power to tax), the financial transfer system (unconditionality of transfers received), financial self-reliance (reliance on own-source revenue) and borrowing autonomy (independent power to borrow).
Sub-indicators are summed with the index's own point weights (4, 3, 3, 3) and rescaled to 0–1.

The Regional Authority Index measures the self-rule and shared rule of regional governments from 1950 to 2018. Where the LAI assesses the autonomy of local governments, the RAI evaluates the autonomy of regional governments such as cantons, provinces, states or Länder: a federal country with strong provinces but weak local government may score high on the RAI and low on the LAI.
National values are population-weighted means of regional scores, rescaled here to 0–1 from the published 0–30 scale.
The fiscal dimension of the RAI combines two sub-indicators: fiscal autonomy (independent power to tax) and borrowing autonomy (independent power to borrow).
Sub-indicators are summed with the index's own point weights (4 and 3) and rescaled to 0–1; national values are population-weighted means of regional scores.

text: The OECD publishes each indicator on its own schedule, so the sources above are joined on functional urban area and year without privileging any one of them: an observation is kept whether or not the other series cover the same year.

Population is the exception that needs handling, because it is what the other indicators are weighted and scaled by. It is disseminated annually for most countries but only at five-year census intervals for others, Japan most notably, where the published productivity year (2021) falls outside the census series entirely. Population is therefore linearly interpolated between observations within each functional urban area, and the nearest observation is carried forward or backward by at most three years beyond the observed range.

Labour productivity of functional urban areas and the autonomy of local and regional government in nine countries.

The Devolution-Productivity Observatory presents, for Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, South Korea, Spain, the United Kingdom and the United States, the labour productivity of OECD functional urban areas (a city and its commuting zone) alongside two expert-coded measures of subnational autonomy: the Local Autonomy Index and the Regional Authority Index. It is the interactive counterpart of the country profile documents produced for the Devolution project, and draws every figure from the same data pack.

Each view follows the profile: an [Overview](view:overview) of a country's FUAs; [Productivity](view:productivity) rankings, the relationship with population size, the distribution and spread of productivity across FUAs and its change over time; the [Autonomy](view:autonomy) indices; and a [Map](view:map) of any indicator in any year at four geographies: countries, large regions (TL2), small regions (TL3) and functional urban areas, chosen in the top bar. The country is chosen in the top bar; the URL carries every selection, so any view can be linked.

OECD series are retrieved from the OECD Data Explorer SDMX API and joined on functional urban area and year. Population is interpolated between census observations and carried by at most three years beyond them, as described under [Sources](view:sources). Dollar figures are nominal USD at purchasing power parity: comparable across countries within a year, not across years. The reference year for the snapshot views is {ref_year}, the last full year before the Covid-19 pandemic, and the pandemic emergency as defined by the World Health Organization (March 2020 to May 2023) is shaded on every time series.

Means across FUAs are unweighted: each FUA counts once, regardless of population. The fiscal dimensions of the LAI and RAI are sums of their sub-indicators using the indices' own point weights, rescaled to 0–1. The map classes each indicator into quantiles pooled over every year shown for the scope chosen, so a colour keeps its meaning as the year changes.

The site is static. The data are Parquet files segmented by country (one file per country for the FUA series, plus small national, LAI, RAI and source tables) and simplified boundaries (a TopoJSON per country holding its national outline, TL2 and TL3 regions, which share their borders, plus GeoJSON for FUAs), read in the browser by DuckDB-WASM. A country view fetches only that country's file; the cross-country comparisons read all nine. Everything the site shows can be downloaded as CSV from each chart, or read directly from the `data/` folder of the repository with any Parquet tool.

text: National maps show each country's own value
context: Map toolbar, hover box when the switch is disabled
Map hover box, after the value, when colouring relative to the mean

text: Each unit's value as a percentage above or below the unweighted mean of its country's {units} in the same year: red below, blue above, white near the mean. The classes are the quartiles of the distance from the mean, pooled over every year. {variable_label}.
context: Map legend note, relative colouring of a positive indicator

text: Each unit's value minus the unweighted mean of its country's {units} in the same year, in the indicator's units: red below, blue above, white near the mean. The classes are the quartiles of the distance from the mean, pooled over every year. {variable_label}.
context: Map legend note, relative colouring of an indicator that can be zero or negative
